title: Deployment window + quorum fencing for safer hosted API cutovers
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a deployment-window coordinator and quorum-based fencing for blue/green cutovers across regions. The goal is to make scheduled host API version swaps safer by validating capacity, cross-region readiness, and proxy consensus before shifting traffic. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and runbook for a 30-day pilot in two regions.
acceptance_criteria: Window coordinator service can create/close deployment windows and persist metadata
Cutover proceeds only if quorum (>=75%) of edge proxies report readiness and capacity headroom
Automated fallback to mirror-readonly mode if quorum fails within timeout
End-to-end e2e tests that simulate proxy jitter, partial capacity loss, and disk stalls
Runbook updated and oncall playbook tested in a fire-drill with staging traffic
Latency and error-rate SLOs for hosted API remain within 10% of baseline during pilot
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy coordinator as a non-path-affecting control-plane service in staging; integrate with existing orchestrator and routing API. Phase 2: Enable window creation for a single test tenant and perform a supervised blue/green cutover during a quiet hour. Phase 3: Expand to 5 tenants and two regions with canary mirror sampling (2% traffic mirrored) and automated quorum checks. Phase 4: 30-day pilot monitoring SLOs and incrementally increase traffic. Abort conditions: quorum failure for >120s, CPU >85% on serving nodes, or token error spike >3x. Rollback path uses previously pinned model variant and immediate drain-with-fence. Manual abort CLI and automatic fallback paths will be exercised in each phase.
design_notes: We considered a lock-based global coordinator but rejected it due to cross-region latency spikes causing unnecessary aborts.
Adopted a quorum model: each edge proxy publishes a readiness heart-beat with capacity vectors; coordinator aggregates and decides within a window timeout.
To reduce blast radius we will add tenant-priority lists and an evacuation quorum: higher-priority tenants get guaranteed draining before lower-tier during aborts.
Deployment metadata will be stored in a new deployment_windows table in the release-metadata DB with TTL and soft-delete for auditability. We plan to migrate via backfill jobs.
Security: coordinator will use mTLS to communicate with proxies and KMS-wrapped tokens for any sensitive payloads. Security review is required before production enablement.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Quorum model trades stronger safety guarantees for eventual consistency; there is a risk of slow convergence in degraded networks.
Adding coordinator increases control-plane surface area; must harden and monitor to avoid it becoming a single point of confusion for oncall.
Mirroring 2% of production traffic can expose privacy-sensitive snippets; we will enable PII scrubbing and use a minimized token set for mirrors.
implementation_tasks: Coordinator: implement quorum aggregation + timeout policy
Edge SDK: publish heartbeat + capacity vector and accept fence signals
Orchestrator integration: accept coordinator decisions and trigger model swap with drain tokens
DB: migration script for deployment_windows table and backfill tool
CLI: manual abort/force-close commands and status inspect
Tests: unit, integration in staging, chaos monkey scenarios
Runbook: oncall steps, metrics dashboard, rollback checklist
